It's got a story, the combat is fun, the weapon upgrade paths feel unique, the game feels like it is constantly opening up more and more as you progress the story, the backpack organization/inventory management minigame you play to maximize your artifacts in a run is fun and well done, it has coop.
I really like this game, it is probably one of the most solid roguelikes I've played. I wish there were more game and I wish that the progression was a bit more challenging, but this is pretty much a 10/10 for me.
Don't let the first few hours fool you. The gameplay depth and how the story integrates into it are amazing.
好玩，无需多盐

Some good concepts at work that carry an otherwise bog-standard roguelike. With how little real gameplay variance there is between build types, it's even more disappointing that the fruit stand practically decides exactly how your run will play. You're really just picking between categories, because any two storm cloud or frost relic builds will feel identical to each other.

The base gameplay loop is serviceable, but it becomes repetitive rather quickly. Enemy variety and build/weapon options are too limited for any real longevity. Thankfully, the inventory system is really well done and breaks up the monotony of prolonged combat effectively. It's just a shame that it's the only standout gameplay-wise. The art and music are good, and the story is very low effort. Ultimately, I spent most of my playtime feeling entirely neutral, and the best moments were when I was puzzling out how to make all my tablets and artifacts make sense.

Sephiria is a competent game, but, with the exception of one feature, there isn't anything that makes it feel special. You're not really missing anything by skipping this one.

After completing the game's story, I just want to say thank you for the amazing game, dev. The builds all felt fun in their own way, some more broken than others, but ultimately balanced comparatively to how the game was in beta. Very few bugs, multiplayer and single player felt balanced as well.

Unlockable skins were cute, the story was good, and beating the game felt rewarding and not a steam roll. The difficulty scaling and meta progression felt great and makes every run feel crafted and for the most part, hard to replicate. My only real complaint about the game is the net code and no rejoining when doing multiplayer is ROUGH. Having a lobby crash after 2 hours is heart breaking . . . But the game was so much fun that going back into another run regardless of a d/c softened the blow by quite a bit. It's actually quite hard for me to complain about anything else -- maybe revamp planets or companions to make them more interesting? Or remove them altogether?

9/10, fix the net code and i'd give it a 9.5-10/10

For anyone thinking about buying this game, if you're a fan of gunfire reborn or co op games in general definitely do purchase this, it's very unique in it's own way and you can tell the dev poured a lot of love into this! :)

This game has probably THE WORST button layout I ever experienced.

You go into options, look at the menu, see button layout, push the button to get there...congrats, you just changed the language of the game.

Then you go and actually try to play the game, you get a a grimoire and a skill, both need to get activated from the same casting menu. You have two different buttons you can use per skill. Only one button works...only one button works??? WHAT IS THE SECOND BUTTON FOR?!?!?!

Ok so you can put up to 8 different cast buttons. Good luck finding them on your gamepad. You are already using 13 other button interactions.

So you found 1 or 2 useable cast buttons? Congratulations. Wait...why is the game option menu for button layouts showing you using those buttons, but then you are ingame, the game shows COMPLETELY DIFFERENT BUTTONS. And not just is it wrong in showing those buttons IT ALSO AUTOMATICALLY PUSHES SKILLS IN THEM AROUND WHEN PICKING UP ANOTHER SKILL, EVEN WHEN YOU ARE NOT USING IT!!!


So every time you try to remap your skills you change your language first. 
Then you don´t have a second button menu for fights to use skills. 
Then the game constantly shows the wrong buttons ingame and pushes skills around automatically.
...well it can´t get any worse...
right...right?? RIGHT?????!?!???????
So you use the directional pad or the B button on your gamepad for skills? NO! No, you can´t. That´s not possible. The game doesn´t let you. Those are not viable buttons. YOU ARE NOT ALLOWED!!!

Fine. Ok. SCREW THIS! Then I play the game with only one skill per game. It´s fine. It is super unbalanced anyways (take attack speed, clear the game in one go, take companions or planets or frost, make the game 10 times harder) 
So then you stand there. Fool that you are. Think that you can ignore the useless buttons.
WHY DO YOU THINK THAT??? 
The hub area has a minigame for an unlockable that you can ONLY do on mouse and keyboard BECAUSE THEY PUT THREE CASTSKILLS IN YOUR INVENTORY FOR IT and they are NOT on the buttons that are actually shown to you...or they are unuseable because they didn´t plan that you use a character that automatically deactivates certain inventory slots.

...apart from that it´s actually a good game.
BUT WHAT THE ACTUAL FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF

Have played through the story by now essentially, no hard mode yet.
TLDR: Good game, has some disappointing decisions and questionable design. Worth a buy regardless.

Pros:
Fun gameplay
Great music
Great item/build variety (with a caveat)
Decent story
Balanced gameplay (for story mode)
Good replayability (roguelike)

Cons:
Very clear best items or builds
Enemy variety gets stale
Bad visual clutter mid-late game (i'm sure this is alot worse too in hard mode)
Hard mode allegedly has very little variety due to difficulty

Other balance opinions:
There are very questionable abilities given to you in the game for a roguelike. Essentially, you are allowed to always have items you want at the start of every run, as well as an ability (a character/costume), and even the ability to have item types highly prioritized. Essentially, this all means your runs will be largely the same and almost always similar levels of broken if you decide to do so.

While these are all great things to have, a roguelike's huge draw and reason for dopamine is the high variety and randomness of each run that basically all games have in this genre. You can always just never use any of these, but I argue even giving this option has majority of people including me using them, as there is no reason not to besides giving yourself a disadvantage and challenge. Clearly these are all very intended, you get them early. I believe it's hard for most people to justify not using three game mechanics to better each of their runs, I think it would of been best to leave these out completely, or atleast 1-2.
